correctness.rationale: A full-memory rule changes precisely the identity coset of its source stabilizer H; every output is H-invariant. For the critical reverse fibre, work on B=G/H. If y has a nontrivial stabilizer P=K/H and the changed source p differs only at 0, a nonzero period t of p cannot belong to P: comparing 0 and t would give one changed and one unchanged symbol. If t is outside P, take k nonzero in P. Then p(t+k)=y(t+k)=y(t)=p(t), whereas p(k)=y(0)≠p(0), contradicting t-periodicity. Thus all q-1 reverse recolorings, and only those, have the required source stabilizer. The diagonal follows by subtracting strict transitions from (q-1)M_q(H), using the partition of q^[G:H] colorings by exact stabilizer; this partition also gives the Möbius inversion. In the binary quotients C2 and C2×C2, exactly the odd-sized supports are aperiodic and changing the identity makes the size even. In other quotients the displayed witnesses work: a unique colored site survives with a third color, a two-point support has no period if its nonzero point has order greater than two, and the four-set formed from three independent points in an elementary 2-group has nonzero sum, incompatible with an order-two period. The trivial quotient has q exact-stabilizer colorings and a positive diagonal. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; its finite enumeration is corroboration, not the general proof.

evidence: The theorem concerns generation, including the global binary Klein-four obstruction. Its proof also notes the single exact-stabilizer orbit for a binary C2 quotient. The primary search produced no material additional source; that is not evidence of absence.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Generation and orbit-existence conclusions are not universal enumerations of labeled local rules. Accounting for the C2 orbit issue is important, but does not supply the exact diagonal count for arbitrary quotients and alphabets.

originality.rationale: Credit prior local-action and transition-existence results, the binary obstructions appearing there, and standard Möbius enumeration of exact stabilizers. The supported distinct part is the uniform (q-1)-element fibre over every individually specified output with a strictly larger stabilizer, and the complete labeled transition census that follows. The evidence does not establish priority for the ancillary aperiodic-coloring proportion in isolation.
residual_risks: Broader aperiodic-coloring and equivariant-transformation literature could contain related symmetry bounds or the reverse-recoloring lemma in another formulation; the search was bounded and does not establish universal priority.

value.rationale: The uniform fibre theorem upgrades known generation witnesses to the exact number of available labeled one-step rules for every pair of stabilizers. It determines which stabilizers admit a preserving rule together with the size of that class, and reduces enumeration of all classes to subgroup-lattice coloring counts without iterating over the rules. This is an exact invariant of the same natural maps studied in the generation literature, not a count for an arbitrary small group.
